static_traits.name: Li Wenhao
static_traits.social_status: Has a few artist friends to talk to, but unwilling to discuss self-doubt due to shame; relationships with peers strained by self-criticism
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of similar psychological problems; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly good logic, able to reflect on personal patterns, high cooperativeness, steady speech pace, positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling some progress as an artist, but constantly doubting my abilities, feeling I cannot reach the ideal level, thus considering giving up art entirely. Self-doubt began a few months ago after receiving constructive feedback, worsening when starting new works, receiving feedback, and comparing with others' work.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to alleviate persistent self-doubt, restore creative drive and progress as an artist, ease the resulting significant pain, and challenge the belief that 'not reaching the ideal means giving up' through behavioral experiments and cognitive restructuring.
growth_experiences: Receiving constructive criticism on a piece of work a few months ago; although the feedback was not harsh, it strongly triggered doubts about my abilities, starting from 'moderate stress', with self-doubt constantly intensifying thereafter.

Before and during this, obtained positive feedback from peers and mentors and completed several works I was proud of, and also had artworks sold, but these achievements have limited stabilizing effect on self-worth and are often overlooked.

Frequently browsing other artists' excellent work on social media and comparing; the comparison repeatedly reinforces inferiority and feelings of inadequacy, becoming an important maintaining factor of self-doubt.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough / do not have enough talent
My worth depends on achievements and others' approval
If I cannot reach the ideal standard, it equals failure

special_situations.event: Receiving constructive criticism on a piece of work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others criticize, it means I am unsuited to be an artist
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: By temporarily stopping creating or avoiding continuing the work, avoids further negative evaluations
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves I have no talent / am unsuited to be an artist

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The work must reach my ideal perfect standard; otherwise it counts as a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Procrastinating or avoiding starting new projects to avoid experiencing disappointment again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot reach the ideal, I might as well not do it

special_situations.event: Browsing and comparing other artists' work on social media
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my work is not as recognized as theirs, it means I am inferior to them
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly seeking external recognition and validation to alleviate inferiority
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot compare with them; I am not capable

special_situations.event: Looking back at one's results after receiving positive feedback or completing a work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only sustained high-level recognition counts; sporadic positive feedback does not reflect ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Belittling or ignoring positive evidence, continuing to pressure myself to pursue higher standards
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These good reviews do not count; they might just be luck

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be affirmed and recognized; to be seen and accepted as an artist
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated; the shame and collapse of self-worth brought by criticism and failure
defense_goal: Lowering the risk of being negated by maintaining perfect standards and avoiding creation
Short-term relief of insecurity by seeking external validation

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, an artist who could be negated at any time
object_relations.object_representation: Harsh judges / picky others and audiences

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing work quality, evidence examination, or being invited to focus on positive feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Subconsciously understanding attention and scrutiny as judgment, fearing being negated again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Talking about works and gaps in objective, abstract standards, using few emotional words; emphasizing 'ideals require' and 'standards not met', avoiding direct contact with shame and feelings of being negated.

manifestations: When work does not reach the ideal standard, questioning whether continuing art is meaningful
Binding self-worth tightly to achievement and recognition; feeling hollow and shaken when not yet satisfied
outcomes: Repeatedly considering giving up the artistic path

manifestations: Living alone; ashamed to discuss self-doubt with friends
Relationships with peers strained by self-criticism
outcomes: Passive shrinking of the support system
Self-doubt and shame amplifying in a private cycle

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequently berating oneself with 'I am not good enough / not talented enough'
Before creating and receiving feedback, excessively anticipating negative consequences and shrinking action
Constantly seeking external validation to confirm self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats 'must reach perfection / the ideal standard' as the only valid standard
Internalizes social comparison and others' approval as the yardstick for evaluating self-worth

exception_events.target_problem: When starting new works or receiving feedback, the client typically falls into self-doubt and avoids/interrupts creation, leading to decreased output and increased stress.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In past creative experiences, had completed several works that made them feel proud, and successfully sold some of the works, while also receiving positive feedback from peers and mentors, experiencing a sense of achievement and being recognized.
exception_events.reason: Clue: persisted in completing the work rather than giving up halfway; obtained specific affirmation from peers and mentors; attending to the completeness of the work and the process experience made this self-doubt weaken and produced behavioral output.

positive_force: Has received positive feedback and recognition from peers and mentors
Has the objective achievement of completing and selling work
Willing to try behavioral experiments and cognitive restructuring; high cooperativeness
Having self-reflection ability; able to identify negative thinking patterns
negative_force: Excessive social comparison leading to inferiority
Depending on external validation; negating positive evidence
Avoids / procrastinates creating to escape failure and shame
Affected sleep and decreased drive, maintaining the negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding or interrupting creation (procrastinating, stopping starting/completing works), accompanied by significant self-doubt and anxiety
antecedent: When browsing and comparing other artists' works
When interacting with peers and thinking recognition is inferior to others'
target_behavior.core_reason: Binding self-worth highly to achievement/others' evaluations; fearing failure and shame; avoiding to lower the risk of being negated under 'all-or-nothing' and catastrophic anticipation
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotions (shame, feelings of failure) and potential negative evaluations, gaining short-term security and control
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased creative output, reduced drive, affected sleep; relationship tension with peers; repeatedly considering giving up the art career
